questions.questionText:
To help reduce the price of oil, new supplies are needed. However, objectors oppose exploration
of new sites because of the environmental damage it may cause.
Why is this statement an example of the basic economic problem?

options.text: Oil is a limited resource.
Oil is expensive.
The exploration involves demand and supply.
There are external costs involved in production.

questions.questionText:
Helium is a gas that is limited in supply because it takes thousands of years to form. The US
government holds 35% of the world’s supply of helium and has been selling its stocks. Helium is
essential in medical scanners. It is also used for party balloons, which is a wasteful alternative
use of a valuable good.
Which two concepts apply to this statement?

options.text: demand and supply, government subsidy
excess demand, resource allocation
opportunity cost, private monopoly
public sector, factors of production

questions.questionText: When is production certain to harm society?

options.text: when the private costs are greater than the private benefits
when the production results in externalities
when the social costs are greater than the private costs
when the social costs are greater than the social benefits

questions.questionText:
4
What happens to total revenue as output rises?

options.text: It falls and then rises.
It falls continuously.
It rises and then falls.
It rises continuously.

questions.questionText: What is the role of the price mechanism in a market economy?

options.text: to allocate scarce resources
to increase the provision of merit goods
to make the distribution of goods and services more equal
to reduce the negative externalities of production and consumption

questions.questionText: What is a macroeconomic concept?

options.text: the effect of a price change of a good
the equilibrium price in the market for a good
the reason for a change in a firm’s behaviour
the total spending in an economy

questions.questionText:
The price elasticity of demand (PED) for bottled water is –0.9.
What will happen to the quantity demanded for bottled water if its price increases by 10%?

options.text: decrease by 0.9%
decrease by 9%
increase by 0.9%
increase by 9%

questions.questionText: What will increase the demand for labour in an industry?

options.text: a decrease in labour productivity in that industry
a decrease in the demand for the good made in that industry
an increase in labour productivity in that industry
an increase in wages in that industry

questions.questionText:
Which government policies will both reduce the difference in income between low-paid and high-
paid workers?

options.text: a decrease in the maximum wage and a more regressive income tax system
a decrease in the maximum wage and a reduction in trade union power
an increase in the minimum wage and a more progressive income tax system
an increase in the minimum wage and a more regressive income tax system

questions.questionText:
Wages for nurses decrease, while working hours for pilots decrease.
Assuming other factors do not change, what is the likely effect on the number of individuals
choosing to become nurses or pilots?
nurses pilots

options.text: decrease decrease
decrease increase
increase decrease
increase increase

questions.questionText:
For some months the price of petrol (gas) decreased significantly.
How would this affect a delivery firm that delivers goods for other firms using petrol (gas)
powered vehicles?

options.text: Average fixed costs would decrease.
Profits would decrease.
Total fixed costs would decrease.
Variable costs would decrease.

questions.questionText:
The size of the domestic car industry in Japan has enabled Japanese car producers to be more
price competitive than rival car producers.
What is an explanation for this?

options.text: Economies of scale are present in the Japanese car industry.
Managerial problems exist in the Japanese car industry.
Productivity is low in Japan.
The Japanese car industry is very labour-intensive.

questions.questionText: What is a major advantage of a horizontal merger compared with a conglomerate merger?

options.text: It causes more motivation of the workforce.
It gains financial economies of scale with cheaper borrowing from banks.
It leads to a diversification making the firm less vulnerable.
It reduces competition and increases the merged firm’s market share.

questions.questionText: Recession is when there are two consecutive quarters (six months) of

options.text: deflation.
falling GDP.
rising prices.
rising unemployment.

questions.questionText:
An economy is operating with all resources fully employed.
Which would be an outcome of a significant increase in government expenditure?

options.text: deflation
demand-pull inflation
falling output
increased employment

questions.questionText: What causes economic growth?

options.text: availability of more resources
higher imports of consumer goods
higher unemployment
lower investment

questions.questionText: Which statement about supply-side policy is correct?

options.text: It aims to increase the productive potential of the economy.
It aims to increase total demand in the economy.
It involves changes in the equilibrium foreign exchange rate.
It involves changes in the rate of interest.

questions.questionText: Why is weighting used in the Consumer Prices Index (CPI)?

options.text: to ensure that all items in the index are treated equally
to ensure that all price changes are included in the index
to ensure that the index includes changes in the quantity consumed
to ensure that the index reflects the spending patterns of consumers Due to an issue with Question 22, the question has been removed from the question paper.

questions.questionText: Which combination of policy measures is most likely to increase the level of employment?

options.text: decrease general taxation and decrease the rate of interest
decrease general taxation and increase the rate of interest
increase general taxation and decrease the rate of interest
increase general taxation and increase the rate of interest

questions.questionText: What is a certain cause of absolute poverty?

options.text: growing old
insufficient income for basic needs
lack of good healthcare
many dependants in the family

questions.questionText:
The birth rate in a country is higher than the death rate.
What might prevent the country’s population from rising?

options.text: Emigration is greater than immigration.
The birth rate is falling.
The country’s medical care improves.
The death rate is rising.

questions.questionText:
The table shows statistics for four countries, A–D.
Which country has the lowest standard of living?
average annual
growth rate of population density life expectancy real GDP per head
population (per square kilometre) (years) ($)

Why can specialisation cause economic growth?

options.text: Specialisation can allow a country to produce many different goods and services.
Specialisation can lead to a reduction in average costs of production.
Specialisation can mean that firms in a country will face diseconomies of scale.
Specialisation can reduce a country’s need to depend on other economies.

questions.questionText:
Why do some governments limit the operations of multinational companies (MNCs) within their
domestic economy?

options.text: MNCs contribute to technological advances.
MNCs decrease a country’s unemployment rate.
MNCs gain profits which are transferred out of the country.
MNCs increase a country’s current account surplus.

questions.questionText: What is an immediate effect for a country of a fall in its foreign exchange rate?

options.text: a fall in the money supply
an increase in purchasing power
cheaper imports
